title: Weekend and Holiday Rapid Restoration Blueprint
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This blueprint codifies a predictable, low-friction incident process for weekends, public holidays, and short-staff windows. It prioritizes rapid restoration, clear ownership handoffs, and timely customer status updates while minimizing cognitive load for responders. Use this runbook when service availability or latency SLOs are at risk outside core weekday coverage.

Audience: Oncall engineers (primary), SRE leads (secondary), CS/Support on-call (notification consumers).

Goals and constraints
- Restore customer-visible functionality within the target recovery window: P0 full restore goal = 60 minutes; P1 partial restore goal = 180 minutes.
- Maintain clear single-threaded ownership for the incident commander during the weekend window.
- Use automated tooling (status page, incident tags) to reduce manual communications.
- Minimize handoffs: if incident spans multiple days/rotations, favor overnight keepers rather than full re-briefs.

SLOs and alert thresholds (weekend/holiday specifics)
| Class | Symptom examples | Pager threshold | Target restoration | Customer comm cadence |
|-------|------------------|-----------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| P0 | Total serving outage for hosted API in a region; failed auth across fleet | Pager immediately (phone + slack) | 60 minutes | 0/15/30/60 min updates (status page) |
| P1 | Severe SLO degradation (p99 latency > 2x SLO) or batch job failures affecting background indexing | Pager + slack | 180 minutes | 0/30/90 min updates |
| P2 | Partial feature regressions, non-blocking errors | Slack-only | Next-business-day resolution | 1x status page update at incident start (if customer-visible) |

Ownership and roles (weekend adapted)
- Incident Commander (IC) — single oncall engineer assigned via pager. Responsible for decisions, customer-facing status updates, and declaring severity.
- Recovery Lead — optional; takes tactical restoration tasks (kernel restarts, capacity scaling).
- Communications Liaison — SRE or CS oncall who owns status page text and customer notices. May be the IC if small incident.
- Escalation Board — senior oncall engineers reachable by phone; default escalation window = 20 minutes if IC cannot make progress.

Pre-incident preparations (what to do before extended coverage windows)
1. Run the Holiday Healthcheck (48 hours before): automated script checks KV caches, queue depth, regional load balancing health, and model-serving capacity. Run locally: 

$ ./tools/holiday_healthcheck.sh --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1 --full

2. Pre-warm capacity: run the auto-scale pre-warm playbook for the expected traffic delta. Example command: 

$ ./infra/scale.sh --pool model-serving --target 1500 

3. Create a weekend focused runbook index in Slack channel #ops-weekend with pinned runbooks and owner roster.

Activation procedure (0–5 min)
1. Pager fires. IC acknowledges via phone within 2 minutes.
2. IC posts initial message in #ops-weekend channel with incident-tag, severity, and quick context: 

Incident: <short-identifier> | Severity: P0 | Region: us-east-1 | Impact: Host API 503s

3. Communications Liaison starts a status page incident in the StatusPage system (see templates below) and toggles maintenance mode if appropriate.

Triage and immediate containment (5–20 min)
1. Quick triage checklist (one-pass):
   a. Check control plane health: api-gateway, auth, config-service.
   b. Validate whether rollout, infra job, or third-party dependency changed in the last 30 min (gitops, deploy pipeline).
   c. Confirm scope: single-customer vs multi-tenant vs global.
2. Containment options (pick the lowest-impact action that reduces customer-visible errors):
   - Route traffic away from problematic AZ/region via traffic-control playbook (CLI steps below).
   - Fail open to a compatible model variant or cached responses (policy: only for non-sensitive endpoints).
   - Scale up dedicated pools (for Dedicated customers) per escalation rules in the dedicated-capacity runbook.

Traffic reroute command example (internal tool):
$ rwr --action drain --target az-us-east-1a --service host-api --by 10
(Wait 60s, validate 5xx graph and p99 latency)

Containment validation checklist: monitor 5xx rate, p99 latency, queue sizes. If containment reduces impact, keep IC in-loop and schedule follow-up fix.

Mitigation and recovery (20–60+ min)
- Rapid rollback: if the incident coincided with a deployment in the last hour, prefer rollback to last green revision after safety check. Use: 

$ deploy rollback --service host-api --to-revision <sha> --force-if-empty

- Kernel/driver remediation: for GPU-fleet related incidents, follow the GPU fleet micro-runbook (GPUs should not be power-cycled without SRE approval during holiday windows unless explicitly required).

- Cache priming: after cache flushes, run priming job (CLI example):
$ jobs/prime_cache --model fastgen --top-n 500 --regions us-east-1

- If third-party dependency is failing (CDN, IAM provider), switch to retry policy and circuit-breaker settings for weekend: 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 100ms.

Escalation matrix (weekend adjustments)
- IC -> Escalation Board member 1 (20 min) -> Escalation Board member 2 (40 min) -> CTO on-call (90 min)
- For customer-impacting P0s, automatically page the SRE Manager and CS Director after 30 minutes if not resolved.

Status page and customer communications (templates and cadence)
- Initial status page post (within 5 min):
Title: Service degradation in us-east-1
Details: We are investigating increased 5xx rates for the Redwood hosted API in us-east-1. Our on-call team is actively investigating and working to restore normal service. We will update at 15 minutes.
- Follow-up template (15/30/60 min)
Details template: Current impact: X%; Actions taken: traffic drain to healthy AZ, rollback of recent deploy, cache priming job launched. Next update in 30 minutes.
- Resolution message
Title: Service restored in us-east-1
Details: We have restored normal service and are monitoring. Root cause: incorrect rollout of a config change to the rate limiter. Post-incident report scheduled. Customer action: none required.

Customer email/snippet for enterprise tenants (CS liaison)
Subject: Incident update — Redwood API (us-east-1)
Body: Hello — We're writing to notify you of a service degradation affecting API calls to us-east-1 on <date>. We restored service at <time>. Our team is preparing a post-incident summary for any customers who require evidence for compliance. For immediate questions, reply to this email or contact your account manager.

Post-incident actions and short postmortem cadence
1. Evidence capture: collect timelines, logs, graphs, and deploy metadata within 2 business days. Keep original incident page pin in #ops-weekend.
2. Short postmortem (48–72 hours): IC produces a concise incident brief including timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, and action items. Use the one-page template (appendix).
3. Full RCA (if P0 or if SLA credits are requested): assign an RCA owner and due date within 5 business days.

Game day and practice guidance for weekend incidents
- Quarterly weekend game day: simulate a P0 on a Saturday. Objectives: validate capacity pre-warm procedures, status page automation, and escalation tree. Record scores on the incident readiness dashboard.
- Roles to practice: IC handoff, Communications Liaison rapid post creation, automated rollback verification.
- Failure injection checklist: traffic-shift to a bad AZ, simulate model-serving OOMs, and flip a canary config. Use the staging chaos harness: 

$ chaosctl inject --scenario weekend-route-failure --target us-east-1

Handoff and long-duration incidents (overnight policies)
- If incident remains active across a scheduled rotation, the incoming oncall must be briefed via a 5-minute handoff call with the current IC. If the incident is >4 hours and unresolved, escalate to the Escalation Board before handoff.
- Create a concise Handoff note in the incident Slack thread: progress to date, next steps, blockers, and outstanding action items.

Runbook index and quick reference (pinned)
- Traffic control playbook (commands and quick checks)
- Deployment rollback checklist
- GPU fleet micro-runbook
- Status page templates and automation scripts
- Enterprise customer email templates

Appendix A — One-page postmortem template
- Title: <Short incident title>
- Dates/times: Start, containment, restore, close
- Severity: P0/P1...
- Summary (1 paragraph)
- Timeline (bullet list, timestamped)
- Root cause (short)
- Immediate mitigation and long-term remediation actions (with owners & due dates)
- Monitoring and SLO changes (if any)

Appendix B — Status page automation snippets
- CLI to create an incident (internal status tool):
$ statusctl create --service host-api --region us-east-1 --impact major --visible true --summary "Investigating 5xxs"
- Script to auto-post first update if IC hasn't posted in 5 min (cron):
*/5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/status_autopost.sh --incident <id> --msg "We are investigating — will update in 15 minutes"

Appendix C — Weekend-specific safety guardrails
- Do not perform cross-region DB schema changes during weekend windows.
- Do not power-cycle GPU hosts unless authorized by SRE Manager.
- For rollback: prefer config rollbacks over code rollbacks when possible; code rollbacks require CI health verification.

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: SRE (oncall-and-incident-response) team — maintain cadence: review this blueprint 30 days before major US public holidays.
- Game day owner: Oncall ops lead (Marta Rios).
- Audit trail: update the last_reviewed tag and attach game-day scorecards after each practice.

Where to find related runbooks
- See pinned index in Slack #ops-weekend and the Runbook library: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/

Feedback and iteration
If this blueprint produces friction during an active holiday, file a feedback ticket in the internal tracker with label "ops-weekend-feedback". The oncall-and-incident-response team will triage and iterate.
